A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, equations, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–18, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original LLM behavioral measurements, fitted cognitive-model parameters, posterior predictive checks, and DPO/PPO training trajectories, including appendix results.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results in Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendices C–D. Their retention from v3 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The RSA speaker/listener model, utility components, parameter inference, and training procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds a rationale for equal utterance costs, an assumption already present in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same polite-speech and literal-semantics tasks, vignette framings, communicative-goal conditions, and UltraFeedback/HH-RLHF training datasets. No new dataset or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: The human comparison from Yoon et al., randomly sampled RSA-parameter baseline, and evaluated model/alignment configurations are retained. Comparator membership matches in Table 1 and Figures 4–6.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, reasoning budgets, training epochs, 80% training split, metrics, and sample sizes remain unchanged. V4 newly documents answer-option randomization in Section 4.1; it does not establish a changed procedure or rerun.

E4.justification: Reasoning-budget and goal manipulations, the posterior predictive check, and appendix response analyses are retained without new analyses. The added discussion of convergent evidence cites other work rather than reporting another experiment.

E5.justification: V4 explicitly names the existing z-test and t-tests, but their statistics and p-values are unchanged. Both versions retain four MCMC chains, 2,000 warm-ups and 2,000 samples per chain, and 95% high-density intervals.

E6.justification: The numerical findings and result plots in Figures 3–18 are unchanged. For example, the inferred-versus-random predictive MSE remains 0.03 versus 0.06, with z = -12.49 and p < 0.001; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, priors, utility definitions, and modeling assumptions are retained. The identity mapping for social value is relocated, and equal utterance costs receive additional motivation, without new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions strengthen the sycophancy framing from generating hypotheses to diagnosing behavior and foreground amplification by small reasoning budgets. The central cognitive-model proposal and post-training claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 expands the dataset-selection rationale and interprets persistent base-model effects through connections to pretraining biases. Section 5.3 also suggests future co-training and adapter interventions. Existing domain-generalization and inference limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds code/data access information in Section 1.1 and explicitly documents per-query answer-option randomization in Section 4.1. Hardware, training times, hyperparameters, and appendix sampling details are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds Christian et al. (2026) on inherited value biases and Tsvilodub et al. (2025) on neural-symbolic pragmatic modeling. The broader positioning remains stable; Qiu et al.'s publication update identifies the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: V4 revises the title, abstract, contribution summary, and selected explanatory paragraphs. It introduces numbered model-suite subsections and converts the goal-manipulation and sycophancy subsections to paragraph headings, while retaining the overall organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned as a full-width schematic instead of a text-wrapped inset. Figure 5's caption removes incorrect color references. Other figure artwork and both tables remain unchanged, with limited surrounding layout reflow.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility through the redesigned schematic, corrected color descriptions, documented option randomization, and code/data access information. The empirical evidence is unchanged. Its stronger sycophancy-diagnosis wording lacks additional validation, which the body still identifies as future work, limiting the overall gain.
